Those two terminal strokes extend beyond the e return and support a final s. The following word has a distinct v entry and a low linked erra sequence, giving les verra.

The deletion line crosses the baseline, but the initial two tall angular strokes survive above it, followed by low rounded humps and a short rightward terminal stroke. The same page has an uncancelled Alors with this tall A/l opening and low ors ending immediately before the first displayed integral.

The word begins with an r-like upright and curved shoulder, then has a conspicuous tall crossed t. The following low horizontal connection leads into small joined round and v-shaped humps and a short terminal e stroke, supporting retrouve despite the compression.

The glyph immediately after the raised p has a broad top stroke, a small middle turn and a descending lower curl. It is a single compact xi; there is no intervening d with its own bowl or upright stem.

Between est and la there is a small open initial curve, two extremely compressed horizontal runs separated by short marks, and a long final return rising to an angular t-like end. The medial letter loops and the initial accent cannot be separated securely even in the enlarged contrast view, so the full proposed spelling remains uncertain.
